vulnerable_statements.reason: When btf_type_by_id() fails for relo->type_id, the function returns directly without freeing the 'specs' buffer (~4KB) allocated with kcalloc() just above. A user loading BPF programs with bad CO-RE relocation type IDs can repeatedly trigger this path and leak kernel memory.

suggested_fix: Do not return directly on the bad type id path. Set err = -EINVAL and goto a cleanup label that does kfree(specs). Because the 'out' label also unlocks cand_cache_mutex when need_cands is set (and the mutex is not held yet at this point), either add a separate label that only frees specs, or call kfree(specs) before the return. Another option is to do the type lookup before allocating specs.
